subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session mutations fail closed on legacy ownerless rows across create, patch, reset, and delete, and should this PR own the shared authorization primitive for all those paths?
rationale: Exact equality closes the cross-plugin access boundary, but rejecting legacy ownerless persisted state may break upgrades and the overlapping sessions.patch PR currently proposes the same permanent contract.

options.title: Coordinate exact fail-closed enforcement
options.body: Use this PR's shared guard across all session mutation paths, update the overlapping patch PR accordingly, and explicitly accept ownerless-row rejection after upgrade proof.

options.title: Add an ownerless-state migration
options.body: Keep exact runtime authorization but migrate or diagnose shipped ownerless plugin sessions through Doctor before enforcing the boundary.

options.title: Pause both ownership PRs
options.body: Hold both branches until maintainers define a different durable ownership and legacy-state contract.

recommendation.title: Coordinate exact fail-closed enforcement
recommendation.body: Use this PR's shared guard across all session mutation paths, update the overlapping patch PR accordingly, and explicitly accept ownerless-row rejection after upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged history most directly owns plugin session metadata and cross-lifecycle ownership preservation.
